key_insight: A multimodal digital assessment found that most Parkinson’s disease discrimination came from four upper-limb motor tasks, especially pronation-supination.
clinical_relevance: This supports a shorter, clinically anchored movement assessment that could reduce testing burden while preserving diagnostic signal, if validated in independent cohorts.
method: 31 people with Parkinson’s disease and 30 matched healthy controls completed seven standardized MDS-UPDRS III motor tasks.
Researchers combined surface EMG, inertial motion capture, and musculoskeletal simulations.
A leakage-free machine learning pipeline tested tasks and modalities separately, then fused the strongest signals and selected stable biomarkers.
evidence_signal: The best single task achieved ROC-AUC 0.94, and multimodal fusion maintained high performance with ROC-AUC 0.93 and balanced accuracy 0.92.
watch_item: Results come from a relatively small cohort and still need independent clinical validation before use in routine care.
paper_title: A Reduced Digital Motor Assessment using Multimodal Biomarkers in Parkinson's Disease
